title: Gate 2 closes on machine evidence: preview.decide auto-approves a DEPLOYED preview receipt under a recorded opt-in
description:
SPIDR child B of parent task-d56a0cc5f6ae4dc88da5233a9702d9e6 ("One approval, then unattended"), split 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a. Sibling of child A (task-a47301ee3aa64866ba109d4c0283526f, the mapping + carried opt-ins leaf) and child C (task-24b68b05c865436ead05cd5ea375ff6f, Gate 3 / release.decide). This row is Gate 2 ONLY. It is the FIRST GATE that can go unattended, because unlike Gate 3 it waits on no unlanded evidence row - Gate 3's dossier prerequisite is still PLANNING with 0 commits.

OWNER DIRECTION driving the parent (2026-09-09): "we dont want moe-next to be stuck all the time for user approval we can approve the plan at the start but thats it". One human gate at plan/contract time; the rest unattended, with a human ABLE to intervene but not REQUIRED.

MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a; re-measure before planning:
- `git grep -ln "evaluatePolicy|PolicyRiskTier|autoApprovalOptIns" -- apps/daemon/src/preview/**` returns NOTHING. The preview gate does not consult the policy engine at all today. This row BUILDS that consumption path; it is not flipping on a dark switch. The parent's description called the engine "dark", which is true of the two seams it names but understates this: there is no policy call at either gate.
- The decision function to CALL and NOT reimplement is packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts assessTier at :150-166. R2/R3 return REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with code HUMAN_ONLY_TIER (:155-158); a tier with no matching opt-in returns REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with code AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN (:165). An opt-in matches only when `entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier)`.
- preview-contracts.ts:43 `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND = "preview.decide"`; PREVIEW_DECISIONS is frozen at ["APPROVE","REJECT"] (:63).

THE DESIGN DECISION THAT KEEPS THIS ROW SMALL - do not rediscover it, and do not depart from it without reporting. There are TWO separate shapes and only one of them is a shared contract:
1. THE WIRE PAYLOAD is EXACT-ARITY. decodePreviewDecidePayload (preview-contracts.ts:258-282) demands APPROVE be exactly ["decision","previewRef"] (PREVIEW_APPROVE_PAYLOAD_KEYS :68) and refuses any extra key with PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID. Adding provenance HERE would change a shared runtime contract and force all four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors to rotate - the four-row job epic rail 1 describes. DO NOT DO THAT.
2. THE PERSISTED RECORD is DAEMON-LOCAL and versioned. preview-daemon-edge.ts:62 `PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION = "moe-preview-decision/1"`, PREVIEW_DECISION_KEYS at :64, written at :255-260, read back by readPreviewDecision at :156-190 via exactPreviewRecord. MEASURED: `git grep -n "PREVIEW_DECISION_KEYS|PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION|PreviewDecisionRecord" -- apps/control-room/** packages/control-room-client/** packages/contracts/**` returns NOTHING. Nothing outside apps/daemon pins this shape. PROVENANCE GOES HERE, and no digest mirror rotates.

MIGRATION HAZARD, name it in the plan. readPreviewDecision returns null when `record["version"] !== PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION` (:170) and exactPreviewRecord enforces exact arity, so an optional key is not possible and a naive version bump makes every previously persisted decision unreadable. Recommended shape, to be verified not assumed: bump to "moe-preview-decision/2" with the provenance key ALWAYS present (null for a human decision, the opt-in's action and tier for an automatic one), and keep a read arm that still admits a /1 record by treating its provenance as null. An arm must prove a /1 record still reads back.

WHO SUBMITS THE AUTOMATIC DECISION. Do NOT widen the MCP allowlist and do NOT let an agent seat decide a gate. The automatic decision is taken SERVER-SIDE inside the daemon under the operator principal acting on a recorded opt-in, never as a wire command from a seat. Governor ruling 2026-09-06 (task-136cbab2, comment-b0d0a809c1a7445e91f03f83ea69329d) is binding: do NOT remove a kind from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS - MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS is DERIVED from it, so a roster edit opens two fences in one line. If you find yourself editing a roster you have left the approved scope: stop and report.

A MANUAL REJECT WINS. If a human has recorded a REJECT for the preview, the automatic path must not overturn it, and the refusal carries a stable code asserted WITH its layer. The preview refusal map is CLOSED AT FOUR CODES (preview-contracts.ts comments at :283-292 state no fifth code is minted for a condition the preview vocabulary does not own). Prefer an existing code; if none fits, the correct move is to report rather than quietly widen a closed vocabulary.

OUT OF SCOPE, owned by siblings: the risk-class mapping and carried opt-ins (row A); anything under apps/daemon/src/release/ (row C); the end-to-end unattended journey arm (the parent). Do not widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS or edit packages/core/src/policy/.
definitionOfDone: preview.decide consults the policy engine: a production module under apps/daemon/src/preview/ calls evaluatePolicy from the @moe/core bare specifier and does NOT reimplement tier or opt-in logic; `git grep -n 'evaluatePolicy' -- apps/daemon/src/preview/` returns at least one non-test hit, quoted in the completion record.

An arm proves the AUTOMATIC APPROVE path: a DEPLOYED preview receipt, under a recorded R0 or R1 opt-in whose action equals PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND, is approved with NO human decision, and the persisted decision record NAMES the opt-in it acted under (action and tier), so a reviewer can tell an automatic approval from a human one. Assert the recorded provenance fields, not merely that the outcome was APPROVE.

An arm proves R2 and R3 are NOT auto-approved: the gate stays pending for a human and the refusal carries HUMAN_ONLY_TIER from evaluatePolicy, asserted with its layer. A separate arm asserts POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS still deep-equals ['R0','R1'] and that this row modified no file under packages/core/src/policy/.

An arm proves a recorded human REJECT WINS: with a manual REJECT already persisted and a valid R0 opt-in present, the automatic path does not overturn it and refuses with a stable code asserted together with its layer. Verify non-vacuity by mutating the precedence check in the production module and confirming this arm goes RED; prove the drill's restore by SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup whose path carries this task id, in a call separate from the restore.

The SHARED WIRE CONTRACT IS UNTOUCHED: PREVIEW_APPROVE_PAYLOAD_KEYS still deep-equals ['decision','previewRef'] and PREVIEW_REJECT_PAYLOAD_KEYS still deep-equals ['decision','findings','previewRef']; an arm asserts decodePreviewDecidePayload still refuses an APPROVE payload carrying any extra key with PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID. A full-tree `git grep` of GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST shows no mirror needed rotation, quoted in the completion record.

Persisted-record compatibility is proven, not assumed: an arm reads back a record written at the PREVIOUS PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION and asserts it still decodes (with provenance absent or null), and another arm reads back a record at the new version with provenance present. Both assert the decoded field values, not merely that the read returned non-null.

The human-only fence is UNCHANGED: PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND is still in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and still in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, and no agent seat or MCP tool can submit a gate decision. Assert BOTH directions per global rail 9, enumerating the served set from the dispatch seam rather than only from the roster constant.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXITS 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted and NONZERO, and pnpm typecheck exits 0. pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test is run and quoted as well, since apps/control-room is in none of the root vitest include, pnpm typecheck, or the daemon leg.

implementationPlan.description: Carry PROVENANCE on the persisted decision record - the daemon-local shape, NOT the wire payload. In apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-daemon-edge.ts bump PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION (:62) and add the provenance key to PREVIEW_DECISION_KEYS (:64) so the record states which opt-in the decision acted under: null for a human decision, the opt-in's action and tier for an automatic one. readPreviewDecision (:156-190) returns null on a version mismatch and exactPreviewRecord enforces exact arity, so an optional key is impossible and a naive bump orphans every record already written - keep a read arm that still admits the previous version by treating its provenance as null. WATCH THE LINE CAP: this file is 311 lines against a 400 hard limit; if the change would cross it, put the record shape and its decoder in the new module from step 3 and keep the edge thin. Do NOT touch PREVIEW_APPROVE_PAYLOAD_KEYS or PREVIEW_REJECT_PAYLOAD_KEYS.
implementationPlan.note:
Provenance carried on the DAEMON-LOCAL persisted record. PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION bumped to "moe-preview-decision/2"; PREVIEW_DECISION_LEGACY_VERSION added holding "/1"; PREVIEW_DECISION_KEYS gains "provenance" (always present, null for a human decision, since exactPreviewRecord enforces exact arity so an optional key is not expressible); PREVIEW_DECISION_LEGACY_KEYS keeps the original 8 for the read arm. The wire contract is UNTOUCHED - PREVIEW_APPROVE_PAYLOAD_KEYS and PREVIEW_REJECT_PAYLOAD_KEYS were not edited.

DEPARTURE FROM THE STEP'S LITERAL TEXT, flagged for QA. The step said to put the record shape in step 3's preview-auto-decision.ts if the edge would cross the 400 cap. It would: the edge reached 393 lines with the read side alone and the write side was still to come. I put it in a DEDICATED new module apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-decision-record.ts (172 lines) instead, because the human decide path's record decoder has no cohesion with the automatic decision maker. preview-daemon-edge.ts re-exports every moved name (readPreviewDecision, PreviewDecisionRecord, the version/key constants) so NO IMPORTER MOVES - release-durable-facts.ts:7, gates-journey-fixtures.ts:56, tests/e2e/control-room/lane-preview-arms.ts:23 and the two daemon test files are all unchanged. Same discipline bootstrap-ledger.ts documents for its own vocabulary split. Edge is now 274 lines, down from 311.

MIGRATION HAZARD HANDLED. decodePreviewDecisionRecord tries the /2 roster first and the legacy roster only if that fails; the two are mutually exclusive by key COUNT because both are exact-arity, and the version literal is then checked against the roster that MATCHED, so /1 bytes under /2 keys are refused rather than admitted under a shape they merely resemble. A /1 record decodes with provenance null.

persistedProvenance returns THREE outcomes, not two: null is a LEGAL value (it is what a human decision records), so the area's usual "null means refused" convention would make a corrupted provenance read back as "a human approved this". undefined is the refusal and the caller turns it into a null RECORD, not a null FIELD.

Also added the tracked .js bridge preview-decision-record.js, matching every other non-test module in apps/daemon/src/preview/ (vitest resolves ./foo.js back to foo.ts, Node does not).

Nothing regressed on the version bump.

implementationPlan.description: Add the auto-decision as a NEW module apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-auto-decision.ts. It CALLS evaluatePolicy from the @moe/core bare specifier for the preview.decide action and REIMPLEMENTS NOTHING - not tier ranking, not opt-in matching, not the dominance lattice. It returns a decision ONLY when both hold: the outcome is ALLOW, and the folded opt-in set contains an entry matching the action whose tier covers the subject's, so the record can NAME it. ALLOW ALONE IS NOT SUFFICIENT - the naming requirement in DoD item 2 is what makes an automatic approval distinguishable from a human one, and returning an unnamed approval would defeat it. Anything else returns no decision and the gate stays pending for a human, which is the correct fail-closed default (the engine already answers HOLD_UNKNOWN when no tier-bearing fact is in scope, and REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN when no opt-in covers the action). Keep the module under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
New module apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-auto-decision.ts, 251 lines (under the step's 250 bound after a comment trim; 260 before). Plus its tracked .js bridge, matching every other non-test module in the directory.

IT CALLS evaluatePolicy FROM THE @moe/core BARE SPECIFIER and reimplements nothing: no tier ranking, no opt-in matching, no dominance lattice. `git grep -n 'evaluatePolicy' -- apps/daemon/src/preview/` returns the import at :3 and the call at :124, both non-test.

TWO SURFACES. previewAutoDecisionFor(evaluationInput) is PURE - it calls the engine and reads the verdict back. resolvePreviewAutoDecision(request) composes the 13-key PolicyEvaluationInput against the durable store the daemon's established way (resolvePolicyFact for the single tier-bearing fact, evaluationChain, resolvePolicyWaivers, POLICY_EVALUATOR_VERSION), exactly as validatePolicy does at bootstrap-policy-services.ts:164-192. Nothing hand-rolled.

APPROVAL REQUIRES BOTH GATES, per the step. (1) the engine's outcome is ALLOW; (2) record.riskAssessment.effectiveTier is non-null AND a member of the IMPORTED POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS. Gate 2 is not redundant with gate 1 by design - it re-asks the ceiling question against the frozen constant, so an upstream widening cannot silently widen this gate and a future engine regression letting R2 through is still refused here. The provenance is {action: record.action, tier: effectiveTier}, both read from the ENGINE'S OWN RECORD and neither minted: assessTier requires entry.action === action before it returns ALLOW (policy-evaluation.ts:157), so the record's action IS the matched opt-in's action, and the tier is the subject tier the opt-in's ceiling had to cover.

STEP-3 DEPARTURE, already flagged in step 1 and repeated for QA: the step says to check "the folded opt-in set contains an entry". That set is UNREACHABLE - foldSlices and tierRank are module-private to @moe/core (policy-public.ts exports neither), so reading the folded entry would mean re-deriving `optIns: last?.autoApprovalOptIns` and re-ranking tiers, which the same step forbids. The two gates above are the closest reachable predicate and are strictly stronger than "ALLOW alone".

ITS OWN CLOSED REFUSAL VOCABULARY, WIDENING NOTHING. PREVIEW_AUTO_CODE_LAYERS maps six codes to the layer that answered, derived exactly as PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS derives its own: ALREADY_DECIDED, POLICY_UNRESOLVED, RECEIPT_NOT_STARTED and TIER_UNCOVERED answer at PREVIEW_AUTO_DECISION; NOT_ALLOWED and POLICY_INPUT_INVALID answer at CORE_REDUCER, the same attribution bootstrap-policy-services gives an engine refusal. The preview WIRE map stays CLOSED AT FOUR and PREVIEW_LAYERS is untouched: no refusal here reaches a wire (every one is a returned value, never a thrown DomainRefusal), so widening either closed roster would advertise a channel that does not exist. A declined automatic decision is not an operator-visible error - it is the gate staying pending for a human, which is what it did before this row.

Engine reasonCodes travel with a CORE-layer declination, so HUMAN_ONLY_TIER and AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN are assertable together with the layer that produced them.

previewAlreadyDecided reads the LAST committed result on previewAggregateId(goalId) - the decide edge's own target aggregate - and serves BOTH the manual-REJECT-wins precedence and retry idempotence, because both are "somebody already decided this". One check, not two drifting ones.

implementationPlan.description: Wire the module at the completion point measured in step 1, inside apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-start-command.ts. Two hard conditions. NEVER FIRE ON A REFUSED RECEIPT: the outcome equivalence at preview-receipt-contracts.ts means REFUSED carries a code and a null url, so auto-approving one would approve a preview that never served - fire only for outcome STARTED. AND BE IDEMPOTENT: the async handler can be retried and PreviewDaemonPort.release is best-effort by contract, so a second run must not commit a second decision; lean on the store's expected-version fence rather than a new guard of your own. The decision reaches the runner through the existing PreviewDaemonPort.release seam at preview-daemon-edge.ts:90/:105 - reuse it, do not open a second path to the supervisor.
implementationPlan.note:
Wired at the step-1 insertion point inside createPreviewStartHandler: a new module-private autoDecide(options, supervisor, receipt) call sits after the !read.ok refusal and before the final DurableDecision freeze. preview-start-command.ts is now 220 lines.

NEVER FIRES ON A REFUSED RECEIPT, TWICE OVER. At the call site everything above has already proven the preview SERVED - result.ok held and the durable receipt read back - so read.receipt.outcome is STARTED and nothing else is reachable at that line. Independently, resolvePreviewAutoDecision's FIRST gate is `receipt.outcome !== "STARTED"` returning PREVIEW_AUTO_RECEIPT_NOT_STARTED, so the module refuses on its own authority rather than on the call site being careful.

IDEMPOTENT BY TWO MECHANISMS, neither a new bespoke guard. (1) The commandId is previewAutoCommandId(projectId, receiptId) - DETERMINISTIC in the receipt - so the store's own decision key replays a retry rather than committing twice. (2) resolvePreviewAutoDecision refuses PREVIEW_AUTO_ALREADY_DECIDED when previewAggregateId(goalId) already carries a decodable decision record. (2) is the SAME check that stops an automatic APPROVE from overturning a human REJECT, which is why it is one check and not two.

NO SECOND PATH TO THE SUPERVISOR. The verdict travels through the SAME runPreviewDecideEdge the wire command uses, so the receipt re-read, the REFUSED-receipt refusal, the readGoalLandingStatus gate, the expected-version fence and the PreviewDaemonPort.release stop all apply unchanged and none is reimplemented. To reach the port from the start handler I extracted previewPortOf(supervisor) out of createPreviewDaemonPort in preview-daemon-edge.ts, which now returns {...previewPortOf(supervisor), supervisor}. That is ONE definition of release, not a second supervisor - a port is stateless, the live roster lives in the supervisor, so two wrappers over one supervisor are the same port. Edge is 288 lines.

IT CANNOT CHANGE THE ANSWER preview.start GIVES. runPreviewDecideEdge THROWS DomainRefusal on every gate it refuses; a throw here would turn a preview that started successfully into a refused command, reporting a failure that did not happen and stranding a live dev server the operator was never told about. Every failure is swallowed and the gate stays pending for a human - what it did before this row.

NO FENCE, ROSTER OR ALLOWLIST TOUCHED. This is not a wire command and no seat can reach it: it runs server-side inside the daemon under the operator principal the handler was composed with, on a commandId derived from the receipt rather than supplied. OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and the MCP allowlist are unedited, per the binding 2026-09-06 governor ruling.

Added an optional `clock` to PreviewStartOptions (ABSENT means the real clock), matching the release seam's own convention, so an arm can pin the automatic decision's decidedAt. Production supplies none, so daemon-command-async-entries.ts needed no edit.

VERIFICATION: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck exit 0, no diagnostics. pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test: Test Files 608 passed (608), Tests 10892 passed | 12 skipped (10904), 255.92s. Every pre-existing preview arm stayed green with the auto path live, which also demonstrates the fail-closed default: with no installed EVALUATION slice the module declines PREVIEW_AUTO_POLICY_UNRESOLVED and nothing is committed. NOTE on the leg: a positional path filter does not narrow this suite - both runs executed all 608 files - so the count line above is the WHOLE daemon suite, a superset of the preview arms.

A PRODUCTION DEFECT THIS STEP FOUND AND FIXED - the most important thing in this note. My step-3 selector required EXACTLY ONE installed EVALUATION slice. Measured on the shipped seed world: driveThrough installs TWO (e7a5ee19...=EVALUATION and fff1cc91...=EVALUATION), so that rule would have made the automatic path UNREACHABLE ON EVERY REAL PROJECT while every arm over a hand-built world stayed green. The selector now filters on the DECLARATION - the installed EVALUATION slice whose autoApprovalOptIns name PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND - which is an ACTION EQUALITY used to pick the chain, not a tier judgement; ranking and matching stay the engine's. Two DECLARING slices is still a refusal, because which governs would depend on key order. A committed arm pins the measurement so the discovery cannot be lost.

DoD ITEM 2, positive: over a real bootstrap world with a landed goal, an installed opt-in slice and a seeded operator risk classification, the PRODUCTION createPreviewStartHandler auto-approves with NO human decision, and the persisted record is read back through readPreviewDecision asserting provenance deep-equals {action:"preview.decide", tier:"R0"} and version "moe-preview-decision/2". Also asserts the release reached the runner through the existing seam (released === [receiptId]). Two pure arms assert the naming at R0 and R1. NO arm asserts only the verdict - a decision:"APPROVE" assertion passes identically against a human approval and would not test this row's subject.

DoD ITEM 3, tier negatives, driven through the EVALUATION INPUT (the goal form's risk class is prose to the daemon by the owner's ruling): R2 and R3 each decline PREVIEW_AUTO_NOT_ALLOWED at CORE_REDUCER with the engine's own HUMAN_ONLY_TIER in reasonCodes. An R0 with no covering opt-in declines with AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN; an opt-in naming only release.decide does the same; a null tier declines with RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE. Each asserts the CODE together with the LAYER. The block opens with a POSITIVE CONTROL - the same input at R0 approves - so an arm declining for the wrong reason reddens the control instead of hiding inside its own refusal.

DoD ITEM 3, invariant: POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS deep-equals ['R0','R1'] against the imported constant. Rather than a git check (flaky on a shared checkout carrying 11 peer-dirty paths), an arm SOURCE-TEXT PINS the three authority lines in packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts this gate leans on: the R2/R3 branch, the HUMAN_ONLY_TIER code, and assessTier's exact opt-in match expression. An edit to the engine's tier logic reddens here rather than silently widening what this row auto-approves. Measurement that this row modified nothing under packages/core/src/policy/ goes in the completion record.

A FIXTURE FACT WORTH KEEPING: the bootstrap sequence contains NO graph.activate, so readCurrentActiveGraph answers ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT and readPolicyRisk's fifth join can never resolve. Without an active graph every fact stays null-tier UNKNOWN and the fold is HOLD_UNKNOWN - correct production behaviour, and it has its own arm, but it would make every approval arm vacuous. seedActiveGraph builds one and ASSERTS readCurrentActiveGraph succeeds, so a fixture that stopped working reddens rather than quietly making the positives meaningless. landedWorld likewise asserts allLanded is true.

Both have .js bridges.

Each question from the step, answered with the measurement rather than an opinion.

Q: Can the auto path fire on a REFUSED receipt, or one whose url is null - approving a preview
that never served?
NO, and there are TWO independent gates, which matters because either alone is one refactor from
vacuous. (1) preview-auto-composition.ts:128 `if (receipt.outcome !== "STARTED") return
previewAutoDecline("PREVIEW_AUTO_RECEIPT_NOT_STARTED")`. (2) preview-daemon-edge.ts:210 refuses a
REFUSED receipt inside the shared decide edge the auto path routes through. The receipt decoder
makes outcome and url an equivalence (STARTED requires url+pid, REFUSED requires both null plus a
code), so "url is null" is not a separate reachable case. A committed arm drives the REFUSED case
and asserts the code WITH its layer.

Q: Can a retry of the async handler commit a SECOND decision for one receipt?
NO, by two mechanisms, and the step-6 drill proved they are not redundant. (1) The commandId is
`previewAutoCommandId(projectId, receiptId)`, deterministic in the receipt, so the store's own
decision key replays a retry. (2) `previewAlreadyDecided` refuses once any decision sits on
`previewAggregateId(goalId)`. Under the drill that disabled (2), the idempotence arm STAYED GREEN
while both precedence arms went RED - so (1) covers retries and (2) covers a decision taken under
a different commandId, which is exactly what a human REJECT is. The idempotence arm asserts the
aggregate version is UNCHANGED across a second start, taking the version rather than spelling it.

Q: Does the positive arm assert the recorded provenance VALUES, or would it pass unchanged against
a human decision?
IT ASSERTS THE VALUES. `expect(record.provenance).toEqual({action:"preview.decide", tier:"R0"})`
plus the version literal. A human decision records `provenance: null`, and a committed arm asserts
exactly that on the human path, so the two are distinguishable in the durable record by the field
this row added. No positive arm asserts only `decision === "APPROVE"`.

Q: Does any refusal arm assert only that the operation failed?
NO. Every declination arm asserts the CODE and the LAYER together, and the CORE-layer ones also
assert the engine's own reason code (HUMAN_ONLY_TIER, AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN,
RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE). Each negative block opens with a POSITIVE CONTROL over the same world,
so an arm that started declining for a different reason reddens the control first.

Q: Did the record version bump orphan previously written decisions, and is that proven by an arm?
NOT ORPHANED, AND PROVEN. Four arms: a /1 record decodes with its field VALUES and provenance
null; a /2 record decodes with provenance values; /1 bytes wearing the /2 key roster are REFUSED;
four malformed provenance shapes are refused. Not one asserts merely non-null.

Q: Did anything widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS, edit a roster constant, touch the MCP allowlist,
or change the wire payload keys?
NO, all four measured empty by `git status --porcelain` on the exact paths (quoted in
comment-438571d79f0f49c08ae4744eb7b867fb), and each is additionally pinned by a committed arm:
POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS deep-equals ['R0','R1']; PREVIEW_APPROVE_PAYLOAD_KEYS and
PREVIEW_REJECT_PAYLOAD_KEYS deep-equal their exact rosters; decodePreviewDecidePayload refuses an
APPROVE payload carrying an extra key (including the literal 'provenance') with
PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID @ REQUEST; the fence is asserted in BOTH directions with the served set
enumerated from the DISPATCH SEAM (`ports.registry.keys()`), not from the roster constant.
